notes.title: The Station is coming to retail with a deluxe version!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154691/d11273518bb871a4c7dbfbfac955d98d3b162796.png[/img]


We've kept this under wraps for as long as we can bear it - we're coming to retail! Working with a publisher out of the UK, we're going to release a Deluxe version of The Station which includes so many goodies such as:

- A digital environment and art development manifest  
- Complete copy of our game design document
- The full soundtrack to the title 
- A copy of the script with commentary and discussion on the narrative
- Art collection and download code for a ton of art and wallpapers

We don't have a hard date yet but rest assured - we'll update you on it when we have the date locked in.

You can read more of the details at the link below. 

https://www.vrfocus.com/2018/08/the-station-heading-to-retail-deluxe-edition-revealed/

notes.title: Upcoming Features & Patch Notes B1.53.1
notes.content:
Hi everyone, last night we pushed a new patch live for a few bugs that were discovered. 

[b]Upcoming Features[/b]

- Localization. We're currently translating the game into Italian, Spanish, French, German, Russian and Portuguese.

- Testing a "Free Explore" mode so players can explore the Espial without the puzzles or locked doors blocking them. 


[b]Bug Fixes[/b]

- Adjusted Occlusion code to hopefully prevent occlusion issues from occurring again. Very rare cases of occlusion were reported.

- Magnet tool no longer disappears when it is brought out of maintenance

- Fixed Kevin Elliott's name in the credits, and made the title screen credits match the end screen credits. There were some formatting changes that hadn't been applied to the title credits last time. 

- Fixed bug where switching to left handed controls while using mouse locked player camera rotation.

- Tweaked the floating object code to be a pinch more efficient, and to potentially solve the "floating fruit" issue reported.

- Removed the glass door open sound that happens certain time after the players leave the ship in the Entrance.

- Dropped the sound level of the Main Title screen music and the Intro Cinematics 3db.

- Increased the size of the trigger volume for the "Aiden, get to the escape pods" sound trigger
in the upper hallway

- The sound files for the 3-switch touch screen in Engineering now don't have clicks.

- Removed the redundant click sound from the touch screen in the Bridge.

notes.title: 2 Days After Launch - Thank You!
notes.content:
My friends, I can't say how thankful I am for the welcome you gave The Station on Steam! I'm blown away by the support, reviews and messages that you guys are sending us! 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154691/019031d325d1b4bb55ae5965ba1fb4aa893e499a.jpg[/img]

We're so excited to see the positive reviews and we're so glad The Station is something you enjoy! After 3 years working the project I can't express how much it means to know that The Station has been well received. Again, thank you. 

[h1]Here's What's Next[/h1]

1. Right now, our first priority and focus is patching some gameplay bugs to make sure the player experience is smooth. Thank you so much to everyone who has sent us notes on bugs that they noticed - we're going to get these patched immediately. If there are any you experienced, please let us know in our forum page. 

2. We're looking at the potential of localizing The Station into some of the major languages. Once we have a reliable and stable framework, we can begin the process of bringing more languages online. Please vote in the forums on which ones you want to see!

3. A "Free Explore" mode is in the works where once you have completed the game, you can freely explore the rest of the station to review some of the mystery elements you missed or weren't clear on. We're aiming to patch this in a few weeks.

4. I can't give details yet, but we're excited about sharing news about VR soon! 

[b]For those who have experienced the story thank you for coming onboard. For those who have yet to find the time, we'll see you onboard The Station.[/b]

notes.title: Dev Update. February 7th 2018
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154691/9523d17320f02f1e19becd4b0ff0c7f55853feca.jpg[/img]

Hey everyone, welcome to our dev update for February 7th, 2018!

In less than 2 weeks The Station will be in your hands. There has been no time for rest - below is a break down of what we've been up to:

- Last week we completed our release builds for consoles and are doing the final dressing for you with testing ongoing right until release.  

- Finishing touches on all of our development documents that we're wanting to make available to you. The one we're most excited about is our game GDD (Game Design Document) which discusses each decision our team made to produce the final version of our game. It's not often that studios will release one of these but you'll have full access through our steam store.  

- Soundtrack mixing. The sounds of The Station are be composed into a soundtrack that will ready for download on our Steam page on release day.

That's it for our for this update, our next one will be the last before our official release!

notes.title: Dev Update. Jan 5th 2018
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27154691/73ae0457d21d6c0fd8decdb70b7f93ac76173291.jpg[/img]

Hi everyone!

Let me start off by saying that we wanted to keep everyone up to date with our progress, but we entered the dreaded crunch period of game development which is all consuming of time and sanity. Due to factors beyond our control we needed to delay launch but this meant we could get our game exactly where we wanted it, polished and into your hands!

After delaying PC release in July, we re-assessed the current state of the game and are now confident for a full Desktop (PC, Mac, Linux) and console release early 2018. Our team has grown and bonded so well over these past months and we are all very proud of our efforts to finally let our first flagship game out in to the world.

We’re looking forward to announcing our release date very soon.

Again we are truly sorry, we wanted to deliver regular updates and now we are set to deliver a constant flow of development notes and media right up to our release date with bi-weekly blogs made available through social networks and directly on our games website.

Some of the major tasks has been up to for the past 5 months:
Porting and testing for consoles
Lighting polish
Major sound implementation
Working on media content
Promotional content
Testing, testing, testing and more testing! (Have you ever played a game 495 times?)

For now we wanted to show off our final versions of some of the rooms you’ve already seen in previous updates in their now polished stage!

Plenty of exciting things to share are coming soon!

notes.title: Production Update
notes.content:
In the past few months we've been pushing to polish The Station game content and code to prepare for launch on PC, Mac, and Linux. We're incredibly pleased so far as our Alpha and early Beta tests have been very positive. 

We had scheduled the release of The Station for the end of July 2017, but we want to ensure that the game is the highest quality experience we can produce, especially as we want to use it as the basis for founding a studio focused on  future narrative games.

First impressions matter to us - so we're asking for a bit more time to ensure we can launch smoothly. We are pushing the release date of The Station to January 2018 (we will nail down the precise date in January in the very near future).

We apologize for the delay, but we'd rather deliver you the very best possible experience.

Sincerely,

The Station Team
